answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is released slowly only after verified work — a quartz-clear rule that makes one fake identity cheap but a thousand ruinously expensive. Like an opal that reveals its play of colour only under light, honest history accrues over time and cannot be faked instantly, while an onyx-hard slashing rule burns the stake of any identity caught attesting lies, so an attacker pays real capital per sybil and loses it when the fraud is found.
